title: Clinical and Echocardiographic Predictors of Underutilization of Mitral Valve Intervention in Patients with Significant Mitral Regurgitation
content: Background: Mitral regurgitation (MR) is one of the most common valvular heart diseases and is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality if left untreated. Despite guideline recommendations, many patients with significant MR do not undergo surgical or transcatheter mitral valve intervention. We aimed to identify the clinical and echocardiographic characteristics associated with mitral valve intervention. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 1,637 consecutive patients with moderate-to-severe or severe MR evaluated at Shaare Zedek Medical Center between December 2016 and December 2021. Patients were categorized into an intervention group (n = 191) and a conservatively managed group (n = 1,446). Clinical and echocardiographic characteristics were compared using univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses. Results: Among 1,637 patients, only 191 (11.7%) underwent mitral valve intervention. Patients receiving intervention were younger (72.8 ± 12.9 vs. 76.5 ± 14.2 years; p = 0.001), more frequently male (57.6% vs. 48.0%; p = 0.013), and more commonly of Arab ethnicity (22.5% vs. 13.1%; p < 0.001). Severe MR (68.6% vs. 40.1%; p = 0.0004) and prosthetic mitral valve (6.8% vs. 2.3%; p = 0.0004) were more common among treated patients, whereas hypertension, advanced chronic kidney disease, and previous myocardial infarction were less common. Independent predictors of intervention were younger age (OR 0.98, 95% CI 0.97–0.99; p = 0.035), Arab ethnicity (OR 2.02, 95% CI 1.24–3.29; p = 0.005), and severe MR (OR 2.87, 95% CI 1.88–4.35; p < 0.001). Conclusions: Only a small proportion of patients with significant MR underwent mitral valve intervention. Older patients and those with ischemic or renal comorbidities were more likely to be managed conservatively. Earlier referral to dedicated Heart Valve Teams may improve access to guideline-directed treatment.
